metadata.title: Interest Rates, Company Loans and Jobs Move Together

series_manifest.label: Avg Interest Rate on US National Debt

events.label: Lehman collapse: short-term business credit freezes
COVID: private jobs fall from 128 to 108.5 million
Average rate on US debt bottoms at 1.42%
Average rate on US debt back up to 3.34%

explanation.summary: Three measures of the economy: the average interest rate the US government pays on its debt, the short-term loans big companies take to pay bills and wages (commercial paper), and the number of private-sector jobs. The stripes below show every month since 2002: red means higher than a year before, blue means lower. The three do not push each other. They rise and fall together with the economy: when business is good, companies borrow and hire more, and interest rates go up.
explanation.methodology: Average interest rate on total marketable Treasury debt from the Treasury Fiscal Data API (monthly). Commercial paper outstanding from the Federal Reserve via FRED (weekly, averaged by month). Private-sector jobs from BLS (CES0500000001).

key_findings.title: Fall 2008: Short-Term Credit Shrinks
key_findings.description: Commercial paper had peaked at $2.19 trillion in July 2007. By June 2009 it was $1.21 trillion, down 45%. Private jobs fell from 116.0 million (December 2007) to 107.2 million in February 2010.
key_findings.significance: Companies that cannot borrow for a few weeks cut staff.

key_findings.title: January 2022: Cheapest Government Debt
key_findings.description: The average rate the Treasury paid on its debt bottomed at 1.42%, down from 6.62% in 2001.
key_findings.significance: Twenty years of falling rates made a growing debt cheap to carry.

key_findings.title: 2024: The Bill Comes Due
key_findings.description: As old cheap debt was replaced with new debt at higher rates, the average rate rose to 3.34% by June 2024. As of August 2026 it is 3.48%.
key_findings.significance: The average rate on debt doubled in two years, which is why interest costs (see chart 15) jumped.
